papers.title: On the Relationship between Online Gaussian Process Regression and Kernel Least Mean Squares Algorithms
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between online Gaussian process (GP) regression and kernel least mean squares (KLMS) algorithms. While the latter have no capacity of storing the entire posterior distribution during online learning, we discover that their operation corresponds to the assumption of a fixed posterior covariance that follows a simple parametric model. Interestingly, several well-known KLMS algorithms correspond to specific cases of this model. The probabilistic perspective allows us to understand how each of them handles uncertainty, which could explain some of their performance differences.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文为在线高斯过程与核最小均方算法的理论比较，未涉及有限元分析或生物医学应用。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address expensive simulation sampling, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification for physical models, or transferability to implant/biomechanics design.

summary_zh.motivation: 揭示在线高斯过程回归与核最小均方算法之间的关系。

summary_zh.result: 发现多种KLMS算法是该模型的特例，解释了其不确定性处理差异。
summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，纯理论分析。

summary_en.motivation: To theoretically clarify the relationship between online Gaussian process regression and kernel least mean squares algorithms.
summary_en.method: A parametric model for fixed posterior covariance is derived, showing that several KLMS algorithms are special cases.
summary_en.result: The probabilistic perspective explains performance differences among KLMS algorithms in terms of uncertainty handling.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; purely theoretical derivation.
